acceptance.output_evidence: UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, and the construction is the deliverable rather than a shortfall. There is no second verification slot for either consumer to serve: each holds exactly one scalar assigned the whole SecretString, and the secret itself is a bare 452-character PEM with one BEGIN block. A SHARPER STATEMENT THAN 'NOT REACHED', recorded because it changes the remedy: for opal-portal-authorizer this criterion is UNSATISFIABLE AT ANY WAIT LENGTH even after a second slot is added, because getPublicKey() at index.mjs:25-28 has no TTL -- a warm execution environment holds the pre-rotation key for the life of that environment and Lambda does not bound that lifetime. The only convergence mechanism available today is a redeploy that cycles the execution environments. The estate's own statement of this exact mechanism sits at originVerify.mjs:48-54 for the origin secret. The remedy is therefore TWO changes and not one: a second slot AND a bounded TTL.

mutant.description: The claim this deliverable stands on is S10-AC1's 'neither consumer can hold two keys'. The reading that could have made that claim TRUE ON THE CODE AND FALSE ON THE SYSTEM is a scalar holding a multi-key JSON envelope: both consumers assign response.SecretString to one variable, and if that string were itself a two-slot envelope, every source and byte-level reading would stay true while the conclusion inverted. The planted control runs the IDENTICAL probe -- get-secret-value, then json.loads plus a token search for 'current'/'previous' plus a count of PEM BEGIN blocks -- against a secret KNOWN to carry two slots, opal/auth/origin-verify, in a SEPARATE invocation from the target. If the probe could not distinguish an envelope from a bare key, it would return the same shape for both.
mutant.expected: target opal/auth/jwt-public-key -> json.loads RAISES, 'current' absent, 'previous' absent, exactly 1 BEGIN block. Control opal/auth/origin-verify -> json.loads SUCCEEDS and yields slots ['current','previous']. The two must differ, or the absence on the target is an instrument failure rather than a finding.
mutant.observed: target: len 452, BEGIN blocks 1, JSON-FAIL, current False, previous False. Control (separate invocation): slots ['current','previous']. Identical on both determinism runs. The probe demonstrably CAN see a two-slot envelope, so the absence on the JWT key is a real absence.

determinism.method: Every load-bearing read run TWICE with identical inputs and the outputs compared field by field: comp-read --enumerate on both consumer files; the get-secret-value shape probe on opal/auth/jwt-public-key (length, BEGIN-block count, json.loads outcome, current/previous token presence); the positive control on opal/auth/origin-verify in a separate invocation; get-function-configuration CodeSha256 on both Lambdas; describe-secret on both secrets.

surprises: NFRA_OPSEC202609-Z-S100: BOTH consumers of the login signing key are single-slot, so FWD-10's no-sign-out rotation is impossible as the system stands and nothing was rotated. Confirmed on three planes (source @998c79b970, the deployed bundles, and the secret's own bare-PEM value) with a positive control proving the envelope probe can see slots when they exist. The authorizer is worse than single-slot -- its key cache has no TTL, so S10-AC2 is unsatisfiable at any wait length for that consumer even after a second slot is added. The two-slot pattern this face was told to copy is already deployed in the SAME authorizer for the ORIGIN secret, and originVerify.mjs:48-54 states the exact mechanism that makes the JWT path unrotatable.
